# Rust unit tests live inside the file they test

> A test in the file can reach the private function it is testing, and moves with it when the file moves — which is the half no reviewer ever remembers to check.

Applies to `crates/*/src`.

<!-- archwarden:yours -->

## Context

_Everything between these two markers is yours. archwarden never rewrites it._

<!-- archwarden:end -->

## Considered and rejected

- **A sibling spec file, the way the webview does it** (nothing refuses it) — It cannot reach anything private, so it tests the crate's surface and calls it unit testing. The webview has sibling specs because TypeScript has no other option; Rust does.
- **A separate `tests/` directory for everything** (nothing refuses it) — That is where integration tests belong and they exist too — `app/src-tauri/tests` drives the commands against a real tree. A unit test put there stops being one the moment it can only see `pub` items.

## What keeps it

Nothing can. `spec-pair` looks for a sibling file, and an inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` has none. The rule that claimed to keep this was deleted rather than fixed: a rule that cannot be written is better absent than dead and green. It also costs a clean coverage number — assertion machinery sits in the measured file — which is why the gate reads lcov rather than llvm-cov's own summary. Filed upstream as archwarden#178.
